docs.labeled.component: `Labeled` carries a caption ALREADY WRITTEN in the viewer's language. The kit paints no string
a player could read and knows no notion of a language — that is a law, not a gap — so the
caption arrives on the node, localized by the consumer before it got in, and whoever draws
text reads it from here: a HUD widget, a tooltip, the catalog's own tree panel.
Labeled({ label: t("actions.attack") }))   // the CONSUMER's own i18n, resolved before the node
## Why the kit will not translate
A caption that arrived as a KEY would drag a dictionary, a locale and a fallback chain into
every renderer and every wire message. Arrived as WORDS, it is one string riding one node —
and switching the language is the consumer rebuilding its nodes from its own dictionaries,
which it already does for every other reason.
docs.labeled.caption: A button-on-the-desk with its caption as data, drawn on the glass. `style` names a ROLE, never
a font: a role is what a tree can say and a designer can re-decide, while the family and the
size are the theme's answer to it.
Two roles are registered by this story so the difference is visible. Type a name nobody
registered and the caption falls back to the desk's own face rather than throwing — one typo
in a tree must not take a desk down, exactly as a dangling surface name does not.
